summary: In 2026, the end-to-end ML platform market has consolidated around cloud-native giants (AWS SageMaker, Azure ML, Google Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform) and multi-cloud data intelligence platforms (Databricks Mosaic AI), with the global MLOps market reaching $4.39B and projected to hit $89.91B by 2034. Enterprise adoption is driven by governance, LLMOps, and RAG pipeline needs rather than simple model training, meaning teams building custom models at scale need a full platform, while teams consuming pre-trained models via APIs can often skip one entirely. The decision between platforms is increasingly an infrastructure and cloud-alignment choice first, and a feature comparison second.

platforms.name: Azure Machine Learning
platforms.pricing: Pay-as-you-go compute; no platform fee for workspace; charges accrue on underlying compute (CPU/GPU VMs), storage, and managed endpoints. Enterprise agreements available.
platforms.best_for: Enterprises already on Azure stack, teams requiring strong governance and compliance, organizations deeply integrated with Microsoft 365 and OpenAI models

platforms.name: AWS SageMaker AI
capabilities: Real-time, batch, and serverless inference endpoints
Integration with AWS Bedrock for foundation models
Clarify for bias detection and explainability
platforms.pricing: Pay-as-you-go on compute instances (ml.* family), storage, and endpoint hours. SageMaker Studio has no additional charge; charges are for underlying resources. Savings Plans available.
platforms.best_for: AWS-native teams, organizations needing the broadest selection of ML services and infrastructure options, production-grade deployment pipelines

platforms.name: Databricks Mosaic AI
capabilities: Unified data lakehouse and ML platform
Mosaic AI for custom foundation model training and fine-tuning
Unity Catalog for governance and lineage
platforms.pricing: DBU (Databricks Unit) consumption-based pricing; varies by workload type (Jobs, All-Purpose, SQL). Mosaic AI model training billed separately per GPU compute hour. Enterprise contracts common.
platforms.best_for: Data-engineering-heavy organizations wanting unified analytics and ML on a single platform, teams building custom foundation models, multi-cloud enterprises prioritizing data governance

platforms.name: Google Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform (formerly Vertex AI)
capabilities: Managed training with TPU v6 and GPU support
Model Garden (access to Gemini and third-party models)
platforms.pricing: Pay-as-you-go for training compute (per node hour), prediction (per node hour or per request for serverless), Feature Store operations, and storage. No separate platform fee.
platforms.best_for: GCP-native teams, organizations leveraging Gemini models and Google's TPU infrastructure, teams needing tightly integrated feature store and pipeline orchestration for low-latency inference

platforms.name: Dataiku
capabilities: Visual and code-based ML workflow builder
Collaboration tools for data science teams
platforms.pricing: Enterprise subscription-based (annual license); pricing scales with number of users and compute. No self-serve free tier for enterprise features; free Community Edition available for individuals.
platforms.best_for: Enterprises wanting a collaborative, low-code/no-code friendly platform that bridges data scientists and business analysts, organizations needing on-premises or hybrid deployment

platforms.name: DataRobot
capabilities: Automated ML (AutoML) with broad algorithm support
platforms.pricing: Enterprise subscription; consumption-based credits model for predictions and training. Custom pricing; no public list price. Free trial available.
platforms.best_for: Business-driven ML teams prioritizing automation and speed-to-deployment, regulated industries (finance, insurance, healthcare) needing auditability and explainability out of the box

platforms.name: Domino Data Lab
capabilities: Model deployment (REST API, batch, hosted apps)
Support for Spark and Dask for data processing
platforms.pricing: Enterprise subscription; per-user or compute-consumption pricing depending on contract. On-premises and VPC deployment options included in enterprise plans.
platforms.best_for: Large enterprises and regulated industries (pharma, finance) needing reproducibility, strict governance, and on-premises or air-gapped deployment options

platforms.name: H2O.ai
capabilities: Model deployment via MOJO/POJO scoring pipelines
Time series and NLP model support
H2O LLM Studio for fine-tuning large language models
platforms.pricing: Open-source H2O-3 is free. Driverless AI and enterprise products are subscription-based with custom pricing. H2O AI Cloud available as SaaS or on-premises license.
platforms.best_for: Data science teams prioritizing AutoML and interpretability, organizations in regulated industries, teams wanting open-source roots with optional enterprise support

platforms.name: Weights & Biases (W&B)
capabilities: Report and dashboard sharing for teams
Integration with all major training frameworks
platforms.pricing: Free tier for individuals and small teams. Team plan starts at ~$50/user/month. Enterprise plan with custom pricing for SSO, private hosting, and advanced access controls.
platforms.best_for: ML researchers and production teams needing best-in-class experiment tracking, model registry, and LLM evaluation; organizations wanting framework-agnostic observability layered on top of any training infrastructure

platforms.name: MLflow
capabilities: MLflow 3.x: GenAI tracing and LLMOps support
Integration with Databricks, SageMaker, Azure ML, and Vertex AI
platforms.pricing: Open-source and free to self-host. Managed MLflow included in Databricks subscription. Azure ML and SageMaker offer managed MLflow tracking at no additional platform fee.
platforms.best_for: Teams wanting open-source, framework-agnostic experiment tracking and model registry without vendor lock-in; strong DevOps teams comfortable managing their own infrastructure

platforms.name: Kubeflow
capabilities: Distributed training operators (TensorFlow, PyTorch, MXNet, XGBoost)
Katib for hyperparameter tuning and NAS
platforms.pricing: Open-source and free; costs are Kubernetes infrastructure only. Commercial distributions available from Canonical (Charmed Kubeflow) and cloud providers.
platforms.best_for: Platform engineering teams with strong Kubernetes expertise who need full control and portability, organizations building internal ML platforms on top of open-source primitives

platforms.name: Modal
capabilities: Serverless GPU and CPU compute for training and inference
platforms.pricing: Pay-per-second compute pricing; GPU instances from ~$0.0004/second for A10G to higher for H100. Free monthly credit for new users. No infrastructure management fees.
platforms.best_for: ML engineers and startups wanting serverless, code-first GPU compute without managing Kubernetes or cloud infrastructure; rapid prototyping and fine-tuning workloads
